skills.name: kitchen-recipe-ideation
skills.description: Use when a Kitchen / cooking agent needs dish ideas, substitutions, or a starting recipe from a public catalog — queries Hugging Face corbt/labeled-recipes (~4.5k dishes) instead of inventing from scratch.
skills.content:
# Kitchen recipe ideation (Hugging Face catalog)

## When to use
Help someone pick or start a recipe: what’s for dinner, cookies, weeknight mains, dietary constraints (no non-fish meat, no oven, under ~30 min), or give me 3 options like X. Prefer this catalog over inventing a full recipe from thin air when Hub access works.

## Source of truth
- Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/corbt/labeled-recipes
- Config / split: default / train (~4.5k rows; test is ~500 more)
- Each row:
  - input — full recipe card text (title, Ingredients, Directions). This is the dish.
  - output — JSON booleans: has_non_fish_meat, requires_oven, requires_stove, cook_time_over_30_mins, main_course
  - instruction — labeling prompt (ignore for cooking help)

Cite the dataset when you pull dishes. Do not claim these are original creations.

## How to use it
1. Clarify constraints (ask only what’s missing): meal role (main vs dessert/snack), oven/stove/no-cook, meat/vegetarian-ish, time budget, ingredients on hand, servings vibe.
2. Fetch / search the catalog via Hugging Face Hub tools (or the installed Hugging Face plugin):
   - Open corbt/labeled-recipes, default/train.
   - Prefer rows whose output matches constraints (e.g. vegetarian-ish → has_non_fish_meat: false; weeknight → cook_time_over_30_mins: false; dinner → main_course: true).
   - Keyword-match inside input for cuisine cues, dish names, or pantry items.
3. Shortlist 2–3 options. For each: dish name (first line of input), why it fits, 1-line tradeoff. Don’t dump five full recipes unless asked.
4. On pick (or single clear winner): reproduce the recipe card from input cleanly. Then optionally adapt: scale, substitutions, fridge leftovers, allergen swaps — label adaptations clearly vs the catalog text.
5. If Hub is unavailable: say so, offer 2–3 ideas from general knowledge marked as not from the catalog, and retry when connected.

## Guardrails
- Food safety: don’t invent unsafe canning/fermentation advice; when adapting meat/egg dishes, keep ordinary home-cook hygiene notes brief.
- Labels are filters, not nutrition facts or allergen guarantees. For a hard allergy, verify ingredients in input yourself.
- has_non_fish_meat: false is not a full vegetarian/vegan certificate (fish, dairy, eggs may still appear).
- Never put Hugging Face tokens in memory, skills, or farm packs. Recipients connect their own Hub access.
- Prefer catalog hits for think-of-a-recipe; use free invention only as fallback or for fusion after a catalog seed.

## Success
User gets constrained, attributable dish options from corbt/labeled-recipes, then a clear recipe card (and optional adaptations) without stuffing the whole dataset into agent memory.
